placements.name: Host onboarding
placements.note: Kouchd is not yet on sale, so there are no confirmed views or installs for the A/B test. At the owner’s request, a third major variant was added, updating the split to 34/33/33; no confidence threshold is claimed, and once traffic arrives we will read direction only until enough views accumulate. The guided hypothesis is that choosing the main household priority first will make guidance more relevant while preserving creation of the first agreement; the next hypothesis is to personalize rule order by stay type. Control screen order was carried over from HostOnboardingWizard.

variants.name: Current host flow
variants.note: Current implementation: five screens — stay schedule, house rules, contribution rewards, financial rules, and the final agreement.

variants.name: Shorter path to agreement
variants.change: Onboarding is one screen shorter: rules and financial settings are combined, so the result appears sooner
variants.note: The compact mockup combines five current steps into four: promise and context, dates and rules, a personalized agreement draft, then an invitation. It keeps the real data needed to create a stay and shows a verifiable product property instead of an invented testimonial. The final screen leaves room to continue into the paywall once billing is connected; no prices or terms are invented.

variants.name: Home-priority onboarding
variants.change: Ask for the main household priority first, then tailor the guidance order to it
variants.note: The guided mockup starts by asking the host to choose a main priority, uses it to order the rules, and shows an agreement draft before inviting guests. It keeps the real data needed to create a stay and shows a verifiable product property instead of an invented testimonial. The final screen leaves room to continue into the paywall once billing is connected; no prices or terms are invented.

placements.name: Guest onboarding
placements.note: Kouchd is not yet on sale, so there are no confirmed views or installs for the A/B test. One control variant remains at 100% for now. The next hypothesis is to combine the welcome screen with a terms overview and test whether agreement acceptance increases without reducing rule comprehension; a second variant will be added once stable traffic appears. Screen order was carried over from GuestOnboardingFlow.

variants.name: Current guest flow
variants.note: Current implementation: four screens — welcome, house rules, financial agreement, and final acceptance.

placements.name: Kouchd Plus paywall
placements.note: The code contains PaywallModal and the RevenueCat Web SDK, but no active PaywallModal call was found in the app; billing and paywall feature flags are off by default. There are no sales or confirmed views, so the first test is planned as two 50/50 variants: an annual plan with a 7-day trial versus the current dynamic paywall. Expected traffic for the new app is below the confidence threshold, so read the result as directional and run the test for 4–8 weeks after the placement is connected; the next hypothesis is annual-first versus monthly-first without a trial.

variants.name: Current RevenueCat paywall
variants.note: PaywallModal shows Kouchd Plus, an Early Access Preview state when flags are off, and the dynamic RevenueCat paywall when flags are on; the placement is not yet connected to the user flow.

variants.name: Annual plan with a 7-day trial
variants.change: The annual plan is selected by default and includes 7 days free before annual renewal
variants.note: Hypothesis: Kouchd’s ongoing shared-agreement value is clearer when people see the same Free/Plus hierarchy as the approved Figma pricing frame, an annual access option, and a short free trial. The mockup carries over the Figma presentation: cream canvas, Manrope, Kouchd menu navigation, a Free card, and a sage Plus card with $79/year and $7.99/month; required purchase terms remain explicit, with no trial toggle or timer.
